newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar sheds 75 basis points at close.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar sheds 75 basis points at close.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended sharply weaker on Thursday led down by a weaker Australian currency and strong selling out of the Far East.
The kiwi dropped 75 basis points on the day against the greenback closing at 0.6981/88.
On the Trade Weighted Index it was 21 basis points lower at 68.52.
"There were very high volumes and the Aussie dollar led the way down," a senior bank forex manager said.
A chief dealer said a speech by Reserve Bank governor Don Brash at lunchtime failed to underpin the currency. He said the market had expected Brash to say interest rates had fallen far enough.
"The market may have been long going into Brash's speech looking for him to make statements supporting interest rates and hence the currency, and he didn't.

"Even though rates have not come off the forex market was probably long going into that and the Aussie dollar coming off didn't help. Then there was some TWI selling around that 68.80 level so it really all combined to get through US$0.7010. Once
it got through there it was really stop losses all the way to 0.6980," the chief dealer said.
The senior manager said the kiwi gapped down and back up again on Brash's speech depending on the headlines coming out on the screens.
"Then we saw some reasonably good selling out of the Far East but at these lower levels we have seen some pretty good local buying interest underpinning it at around the 0.6980 level."
He said the kiwi was sold off most nights in the U.S. so there was a chance it could drift down overnight.
